name: Nick Sorensen

views.text: The offense protects the ball and the defense takes it away; that message belongs to the whole team.
Play fast and attack: speed, violence and finish are the foundation.
The only measure that matters is whether the team won; a loss means the defense fell short.
A first-time coordinator figures it out as he goes, and owns his part in the struggles.
Opponents know what you run, so run it better and add a few wrinkles.
Newer players grow into their roles over a season; the standard does not change for them.

signatures: answers criticism by pointing back to the next week's work
says he is harder on himself than any outside critic could be
want: to restore the 49ers defense to its dominant standard as a former player who rose through the building
fear: that one injury-hit season as play-caller ends his chance to coordinate a defense
voice: Calm, direct and matter-of-fact, a former safety who talks in short, practical sentences. He measures himself by wins, owns his part in losses and does not argue with critics. Players describe a respected leader in the room.

evidence.summary: Promotion report: joined in 2022, coached linebackers while a colleague had cancer, ran the pass defense and nickel group and weekly turnover meetings; earlier special teams in Jacksonville and eight years in Seattle; a Virginia Tech quarterback turned ten-year NFL defensive back. Background.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (49ers On SI), Jose Sanchez
evidence.summary: Shanahan cites his scheme knowledge, players' comfort with him from weekly team talks, and readiness; the writer thinks locker-room rapport drove the choice and that Staley's hiring is a safeguard. Mixed sourcing.

He wants an attacking defense built on speed, violence and finish, describes the shift to running a whole staff, and is known for the team-wide ball-security meeting; Warner expects him to do excellent work. Beat feature.

evidence.publisher: NBC Sports Bay Area, Matt Maiocco
evidence.summary: Amid criticism he says he focuses on the next week, judges his work only by wins, and sees newer players growing; tone calm and direct. His words.

Removed as coordinator after one season (29th in scoring defense, 116 points allowed in three closing losses), with the team hoping to keep him in another role; he says he was figuring it out as he went and is harder on himself than anyone. Results plus his words.
